variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: Coordinates are [y, x]. The right-side target is the one with the SMALLER x; the left-side target is the one with the LARGER x. First read the goal to get the required number of target visits REQ: if it says 'repeating this back and forth motion N times' then REQ = 2*N (two=4, three=6); if it instead says 'then put it down on the left-side target' then REQ = 2. Every episode starts with subgoal A. At each decision step FIRST update visits_done from what the step shows (per the memory instruction), THEN apply every rule below to the UPDATED value, never the carried-in one. Rules (apply whichever matches the current step and memory): 0. Every test below of cube state ('held' or 'not held'), finger opening, gripper height and target highlighting is applied to the LAST frame shown, the scene at the decision step. The earlier frames are the previous command being executed and are already finished; they never decide the subgoal. 'Held' means the last frame literally says the cube 'is held in the gripper'; if it omits that phrase and the fingers are 100% open, the cube is on the table. 1. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and visits_done is 0 (cube resting on the table, fingers open, nothing done yet): choose A, pick up the cube, pointing at the cube's center coordinates. 2. If the cube IS held in the gripper and visits_done < REQ: choose B, move to the top of the target. Pointing rule: if a highlighted target is visible in the scene, point at the target that is NOT highlighted (its listed coordinates); the highlighted one is the target just reached and is never the point. If no target is highlighted (just after pick-up), point at the right-side target (smaller x). As a check only, the updated visits_done parity should agree: even (0, 2, 4...) means the point is the right-side target, odd (1, 3, 5...) the left-side target. 3. If the cube IS held in the gripper and the updated visits_done >= REQ (the cube is now above the left-side target after the last required visit): choose C, put the cube on the table. 4. If the cube is NOT held in the gripper and the updated visits_done >= REQ (cube resting on the table after the put-down, fingers fully open, gripper raised): choose D, press the button. If no rule matches: when the cube is held, choose B pointing at the target that is not highlighted; when the cube is on the table and visits_done is 0, choose A at the cube; when the cube is on the table and visits_done > 0, choose D.

fields.name: visits_done
fields.description: If the carried-in memory is empty (first decision step), write visits_done=0 explicitly as this step's memory. Otherwise carry in the previous value. Compute this field BEFORE choosing the subgoal; the subgoal rules read the updated value. Look ONLY at the last frame shown (the scene at this decision step). Add 1 if and only if that last frame says the cube 'is held in the gripper' AND lists a 'highlighted target' under the gripper (its x within about 15 of the gripper's x). Do not look at earlier frames of the step for this test; whether the highlight was already present earlier in the step is irrelevant, one such final scene is one arrival. Do not add when the last frame shows the cube held with no highlighted target (the pick-up step), or when the last frame does not say 'is held' (put-down done, or button step). Otherwise keep the carried-in value unchanged (the pick-up step, the put-down step where the cube ends on the table with fingers fully open, and the press-button step do not change it). e.g. 3
fields.annotation: Number of completed 'move to the top of the target' subgoals so far in the episode, counting each arrival of the held cube over a target (right or left). It is 0 at the first step (written explicitly as 0, never left blank) and stays 0 through the step that ends the pick-up. It increases by exactly 1 at each decision step that ends a B subgoal, i.e. every decision step whose final scene shows the cube held in the gripper with exactly one target listed as 'highlighted target' directly below the gripper (its x within about 15 of the gripper's x). Only the final scene of the step is read for this test; earlier frames of the step are ignored, and it is irrelevant whether the highlight was already present in them. Each such step is one arrival, since every 'move to the top of the target' subgoal ends with exactly one new target under the held cube. The first such step takes it from 0 to 1. Where both targets appear highlighted in a mid-step frame, only the final scene counts. It does not change at the step that ends the put-down (cube no longer held) or at the press-button step. e.g. 3

history.critique:
field visits_done, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Keep the field, but state its moment of change by the scene alone so that the policy half can be written the same way. visits_done holds the number of arrivals of the held cube above a target so far. It is 0 at the first step and through the pick-up step. It increases by 1 at every decision step whose final scene shows the cube held in the gripper with a highlighted target directly below the gripper (same x region), when that target was shown as a plain, un-highlighted target in the first execution frame of the step (or no highlighted target was shown at all). The fact that only plain targets were listed early in the step and a highlighted target is listed at the end is itself the arrival. It never changes at the step where the cube is released onto the table or at the press-button step. Example: 1 after the first arrival over the right-side target.

field visits_done, POLICY PROMPT
  Carried-in value, 0 when memory is empty. Compute this field BEFORE choosing the subgoal. Add 1 exactly when the scene of this decision step shows the cube 'held in the gripper' and lists a 'highlighted target' under the gripper, while the first execution frame shown for this step listed that same position only as a plain 'target' or listed no highlighted target at all. The typical case is the first arrival: the earlier frames of the step list only plain targets and the final frames list one highlighted target; that is an increment, from 0 to 1. Keep the value when the highlighted target in the final scene is the same one that was already highlighted in the first frame, when the cube is not held (pick-up not yet closed, or cube released on the table with fingers fully open), and at the press-button step. Example: 1.
